blocks.title: 1. What Is GST?
blocks.content:
GST (Goods & Services Tax) is a **single, unified indirect tax** levied on the supply of goods and services across India.

Before GST, there were many separate taxes — VAT, service tax, excise duty, etc. GST replaced them all with **one tax system**.

GST is always calculated as a **percentage of the selling price** (or the marked price / listed price of the item).

blocks.title: 2. Structure: CGST, SGST & IGST
blocks.content:
GST is split into components depending on the type of transaction:

**Within the same state (Intra-state):**
• **CGST** (Central GST) → goes to the Central Government
• **SGST** (State GST) → goes to the State Government
• CGST rate = SGST rate = half of the total GST rate

**Between different states (Inter-state):**
• **IGST** (Integrated GST) → goes to the Central Government, then shared
• IGST rate = full GST rate

**Example:** If GST is 18%, then CGST = 9% and SGST = 9% for intra-state sales.

blocks.title: 3. Calculating GST Amount
blocks.content:
The GST amount is calculated on the **selling price** (before tax).

**Formula:**
GST Amount = (Selling Price × GST Rate) ÷ 100

**Total Price (with GST):**
Total = Selling Price + GST Amount

**Example:**
A laptop costs ₹50,000 and GST is 18%.
GST Amount = 50,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = ₹9,000
Total Price = 50,000 + 9,000 = **₹59,000**

For intra-state: CGST = ₹4,500, SGST = ₹4,500.

blocks.title: 4. Input Tax Credit (ITC)
blocks.content:
**Input Tax Credit** means: if you are a business, you can **subtract** the GST you already paid on purchases (inputs) from the GST you collect on sales (output).

**Formula:**
GST Payable = Output GST − Input GST

**Example:**
A shopkeeper buys goods for ₹1,000 + 18% GST = ₹180 (input GST).
He sells them for ₹1,500 + 18% GST = ₹270 (output GST).
GST payable to government = 270 − 180 = **₹90**.

This avoids the **cascading effect** (tax on tax) that existed before GST.

blocks.title: 5. Common Mistakes
blocks.content:
**Mistake 1:** Calculating GST on the total price instead of the base price.
→ GST is always on the **pre-tax price**, not the final amount.

**Mistake 2:** Confusing the total GST rate with CGST/SGST rates.
→ If GST = 12%, then CGST = 6% and SGST = 6%. Don't apply 12% twice!

**Mistake 3:** Forgetting to add both CGST and SGST to get the total.
→ Total tax = CGST + SGST (for intra-state) or just IGST (for inter-state).

**Mistake 4:** Mixing up input and output tax in ITC questions.
→ Input = what you paid; Output = what you collected.
